citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Most serious cases are those in which the trunk is involved.]

category: Appraise causes of death due to burn
front: Q: List the chronological complications leading to death from thermal burns.
back:
1. Immediate: Primary shock (pain/fear).
2. Secondary: Secondary shock (fluid loss/hemoconcentration).
3. Delayed: Toxemia (24–36 hours) or Septicemia (after several days).
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Chronological complications upon the body as a whole are: Immediate primary shock due to pain. Secondary shock with circulatory collapse due to loss of fluid and hemo-concentration. Death occurs: either within 24-36 hours due to toxemia... or after many days, due to infection and septicemia.

category: Appraise causes of death due to burn
front: Q: Explain the pathophysiological mechanism of 'Secondary Shock' in burn fatalities.
back: Massive loss of plasma and fluids from the burnt surface leads to hemoconcentration and circulatory collapse.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Secondary shock with circulatory collapse due to loss of fluid and hemo-concentration.

category: Appraise causes of death due to burn
front: Q: Differentiate the timeframe of death due to Toxemia versus Septicemia in burns.
back: Toxemia causes death within 24–36 hours due to tissue toxins. Septicemia causes death after several days due to infection.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Death occurs: either within 24-36 hours due to toxemia (production of toxins by burnt tissue) OR after many days, due to infection and septicemia.

category: Appraise causes of death due to burn
front: Q: What is the likely cause of death if a burn victim expires within minutes?
back: Primary Shock. This is a neurogenic shock resulting immediately from intense pain or sudden fear.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Immediate primary shock due to pain.

category: Appraise causes of death due to burn
front: Q: Define the origin of 'Toxemia' as a cause of death in thermal burns.
back: It results from the production and systemic absorption of toxins generated by the burnt and damaged tissues.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Death occurs: either within 24-36 hours due to toxemia (production of toxins by burnt tissue).

category: Appraise causes of death due to burn
front: Q: Which specific gastrointestinal finding is characteristic of severe stress in fatal burns?
back: Curling's ulcers. These are acute erosions in the gastric and duodenal mucosa caused by severe pain and stress.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Curling ulcers develop in gastric and duodenal Mucosa, which occur due to pain and stress.

category: Appraise causes of death due to burn
front: Q: How does the anatomical distribution of burns influence the risk of death?
back: Involvement of the trunk is considered the most serious and carries the highest mortality risk.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): Most serious cases are those in which the trunk is involved.

category: Appraise causes of death due to burn
front: Q: Identify the respiratory evidence confirming a victim was alive during a fire.
back: Presence of black sooty particles in the trachea/bronchi and blood carbon monoxide levels exceeding 70%.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach and the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood... are strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe.

category: Appraise causes of death due to burn
front: Q: Explain the physiological loop connecting secondary shock to eventual renal failure.
back: Circulatory collapse from fluid loss causes renal ischemia, as the kidneys attempt to excrete acidic metabolites from damaged muscles.
citation: Page 84 (Book Page): [Crush syndrome] is due to attempt on the part of kidney to excrete acid metabolites from damaged muscles... due to renal ischemia.

category: Appraise causes of death due to burn
front: Q: What percentage of total body surface area (TBSA) involvement is typically fatal?
back: A fatal outcome is usually expected when the burnt area exceeds one-third (33%) of the total body surface.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): Fatal outcome from burns occurs, when involved area is more than one third of total body surface.

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What is the most reliable external naked-eye sign of an ante-mortem burn?
back:
* Well-marked reddening (Red line of demarcation).
* Roughly 1/4 inch in width bordering the lesion.
* Indicates a vital inflammatory response.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Heated objects and flame produce well marked reddening, 1/4 inch in width, bordering the lesion]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Explain the enzyme histochemical advantage in determining the age of a burn.
back:
* Increase in enzyme reaction at the periphery.
* Detectable much earlier than standard histological changes.
* Stable enough to withstand post-mortem delay.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Increase in enzyme reaction at the periphery of the burn, which can be detected much earlier than histological changes.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Contrast ante-mortem blisters from post-mortem heat blisters.
back:
* AM: Contain plasma exudate rich in albumin; raw skin surface is pink.
* PM: Contain mainly air or steam; lack vital reaction; base is dry and yellow.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Pressure steam and liquids at high temperature cause blisters having plasma exudate containing albumin. Raw Skin Surface is pink]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Which autopsy findings in the respiratory tract confirm the victim was alive during a fire?
back:
* Presence of black sooty particles in the trachea and bronchi.
* Carbon monoxide (CO) saturation >70% in the blood or bone marrow.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach and the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood and other tissue like bone-marrow are strong evidence of an ante- mortem catastrophe.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Name the four specific enzymes studied to differentiate ante-mortem from post-mortem burns.
back:
1. Alkaline phosphatase.
2. Acid phosphatase.
3. Leucine amino-peptidase.
4. Non-specific esterase.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Chosen study enzymes were alkaline phosphatase, acid phosphatase, Lucien amino- peptidase and non-specific esterase.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What defines a 'superficial' versus 'deep' burn in forensic certification?
back:
* Superficial: Does not involve the full thickness of the skin.
* Deep: Involves the full thickness of the skin and underlying deeper tissues.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Generally two depths are referred to in the medical certificate; superficial, which does not involve full thickness of skin and others, which involve full thickness of skin and deeper tissues.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What is the significance of 'pugilistic attitude' in a charred corpse?
back:
* Boxer-like posture due to heat coagulation of flexor muscle proteins.
* It is a post-mortem artifact.
* Found in both AM and PM burning; does not prove the victim was alive.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Dead body acquires a specific boxer attitude called pugilistic attitude due to heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscle proteins. Finding has no significance, as even a dead body will attain it.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: How is a post-mortem 'Heat Hematoma' distinguished from a traumatic extra-dural hemorrhage?
back:
* Heat Hematoma: Light in color with a characteristic 'honeycomb' appearance.
* Location: Found in the immediate vicinity of external heat-induced skull burns.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [extra-dural heat hematoma, in the immediate vicinity of external burn of head. This hematoma is light in color and has a honeycomb appearance.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: In the chronology of burn complications, what typically causes death after 24–36 hours?
back:
* Toxemia.
* Resultant from the production of toxins by the burnt tissue.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Death occurs either within 24-36 hours due to toxemia (production of toxins by burnt tissue) or after many days, due to infection and septicemia]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Describe the expected timeline for the appearance of 'erythema' and 'pus' in a burn.
back:
* Erythema: Appears at once (initial redness).
* Pus/Granulation: Typically appears after several days following infection.
citation: Page 62 (Book Page): [Progressive stages of thermal lesion are redness, which appears at once... After few hours, there will be leucocytes infiltration... followed by appearance of pus and granulation tissue.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
coreConcept: Naked-Eye Vital Reactions in Ante-mortem Burns
front: Q: List the three primary naked-eye vital reactions indicating an ante-mortem burn.
back:
- A well-marked reddening (erythema) roughly 1/4 inch wide bordering the lesion.
- Vesicles/blisters containing plasma exudate rich in albumin.
- A pink, raw appearance of the skin surface beneath blisters.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Heated objects and flame produce well marked reddening, 1/4 inch in width, bordering the lesion... blisters having plasma exudate containing albumin. Raw skin surface is pink]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
coreConcept: Internal and Histochemical Ante-mortem Burn Evidence
front: Q: What internal and histochemical findings confirm the ante-mortem nature of a burn in a fire victim?
back:
- Black sooty particles found in the trachea, bronchi, or stomach.
- Carbon monoxide saturation levels exceeding 70% in the blood or bone marrow.
- Increased enzyme activity (e.g., alkaline phosphatase) at the burn periphery, detectable earlier than histological changes.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach and the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood and other tissue... Increase in enzyme reaction at the periphery of the burn, which can be detected much earlier than histological changes.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What is the defining naked-eye feature of a vital reaction in an ante-mortem burn?
back: Well-marked reddening (erythema), approximately 1/4 inch in width, bordering the burn lesion.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Heated objects and flame produce well marked reddening, 1/4 inch in width, bordering the lesion]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Contrast the fluid contents of ante-mortem versus post-mortem burn blisters.
back:
* Ante-mortem: Contains plasma exudate rich in albumin.
* Post-mortem: Contains air or gas only.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Pressure steam and liquids at high temperature cause blisters having plasma exudate containing albumin. ... Vesicles in most cases do not appear in such burns, and if they do appear, their size is small and extent minimal. (in post mortem context)]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: How is histochemistry used to differentiate ante-mortem from post-mortem burns?
back: Increased enzyme reactions (alkaline/acid phosphatase, esterase) at the burn periphery indicate the lesion occurred during life.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Histo-chemistry at the periphery of the burnt skin indicates increased enzymes reaction ... can be applied for medico-legal distinction of ante-mortem and post-mortem burns.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: In a burnt corpse, what do sooty particles in the trachea specifically diagnose?
back: Strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe, indicating the victim inhaled smoke while alive.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach ... are strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What is the diagnostic threshold for Carbon Monoxide in blood to confirm ante-mortem fire exposure?
back: Presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in the blood or bone marrow.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood and other tissue like bone-marrow are strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: List the chronological stages of a thermal burn lesion used for age determination.
back:
1. Redness (immediate)
2. Blistering
3. Leucocyte infiltration (hours later)
4. Pus/Granulation (days)
5. Scarring/Contracture (months)
citation: Page 62 (Book Page): [Progressive stages of thermal lesion are redness, which appears at once, followed by blistering... After few hours, there will be leucocytes infiltration... followed by appearance of pus and granulation tissue.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: How is the 'Rule of Nine' applied in medicolegal burn certification?
back: It calculates the percentage of body surface area involved to determine prognosis and relationship to death.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Medical Examiner takes advantage of the rule of nine to calculate the extent and percentage area involved bearing burns of the body surface.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Differentiate an ante-mortem extradural hematoma from a post-mortem fire-induced extradural hematoma.
back: Post-mortem fire hematomas are light in color and have a distinct honeycomb appearance.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [extra-dural heat hematoma... hematoma is light in color and has a honeycomb appearance.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Describe the 'Pugilistic Attitude' found in burnt corpses.
back: A 'boxer' posture caused by heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscle proteins; it occurs regardless of vitality.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Dead body acquires a specific boxer attitude called pugilistic attitude due to heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscle proteins. Finding has no significance, as even a dead body will attain it.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What is the primary microscopic finding in an ante-mortem burn?
back: Leucocyte infiltration in the burnt skin, provided the lesion is not full-thickness.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Microscopy: Burnt skin shows leucocytes infiltration, provided the lesion is not of full thickness]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What is the primary naked-eye vital reaction distinguishing ante-mortem from post-mortem burns?
back: A well-marked line of redness (erythema), approximately 1/4 inch wide, bordering the burn lesion due to vital capillary response.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Heated objects and flame produce well marked reddening, 1/4 inch in width, bordering the lesion]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Explain the enzyme histochemical mechanism used to identify ante-mortem burns.
back: Increased reaction of enzymes like alkaline phosphatase and non-specific esterase at the burn periphery, detectable significantly earlier than histological changes.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Increase in enzyme reaction at the periphery of the burn, which can be detected much earlier than histological changes.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Contrast the raw skin surface beneath ante-mortem versus post-mortem blisters.
back: Ante-mortem: Pink, moist raw surface with plasma exudate rich in albumin. Post-mortem: Dry, pale, yellowish surface containing only gas/air.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Table 6.6: Pressure steam and liquids at high temperature cause blisters having plasma exudate containing albumin. Raw Skin Surface is pink]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: In a charred corpse, which findings definitively prove the burns occurred during life?
back: 1. Sooty particles in the trachea, bronchi, or stomach. 2. Carbon monoxide (CO) blood saturation exceeding 70%.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach and the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood... are strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Describe the histological evidence of a burn that is several hours old.
back: Infiltration of leucocytes at the site of injury, provided the burn is not full-thickness (which destroys the tissue completely).
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Burnt skin shows leucocytes infiltration, provided the lesion is not of full thickness]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: State the timeline for the appearance of pus and granulation tissue in a burn.
back: After several hours of leucocyte infiltration, the area may become infected, followed by the appearance of pus and granulation tissue within days.
citation: Page 62 (Book Page): [After few hours, there will be leucocytes infiltration and area may readily get infected followed by appearance of pus and granulation tissue.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What is the significance of 'taches noires' in a fire victim's autopsy?
back: It is a post-mortem drying artifact (brownish triangular sclera) occurring if the eyes remain open; it is not a vital reaction.
citation: Page 140 (Book Page): [Sclera becomes brownish in color and the area of discoloration is called taches noires... Full development occurs in 3-4 hours, provided the eyes remain open.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Differentiate 'Pugilistic Attitude' from ante-mortem defensive posturing in fire deaths.
back: Pugilistic attitude is a post-mortem artifact caused by heat-induced protein coagulation and muscle shortening; it occurs regardless of vitality during the fire.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Dead body acquires a specific boxer attitude called pugilistic attitude due to heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscle proteins. Finding has no significance, as even a dead body will attain it.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Why is carbon monoxide (CO) uptake a critical vital sign in fire investigations?
back: CO inhalation is an active physiological process requiring respiration; its presence in the blood/bone marrow signifies the victim was breathing during the fire.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Victim, while dying in fire, inhales carbon monoxide and sooty material into the air passages of lung.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: When do hypertrophic scarring and contractures typically indicate the age of a burn?
back: These are late sequelae typically seen in partial or full-thickness burns months after the initial injury.
citation: Page 62 (Book Page): [Hypertrophied scarring occurs in partial thickness burn and contracture in full thickness severe burns, which may follow months after the injury.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What is the definitive diagnostic indicator for distinguishing ante-mortem from post-mortem burns?
back:
* Presence of a **vital reaction**.
* Includes reddening (erythema), blisters with albumin-rich plasma, and leucocyte infiltration.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Ante-mortem burn recognition depends upon presence of vital reaction. It is a complicated issue, because there is no sharp line of distinction betweenn the life and death.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Which specific histochemical changes at the burn periphery indicate the burn occurred ante-mortem?
back:
* Increased activity of **enzymes**.
* Specifically: alkaline phosphatase, acid phosphatase, leucine amino-peptidase, and non-specific esterase.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Chosen study enzymes were alkaline phosphatase, acid phosphatase, Lucien amino-peptidase and non-specific esterase... Increase in enzyme reaction at the periphery of the burn, which can be detected much earlier than histological changes.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Contrast the composition and appearance of ante-mortem vs. post-mortem burn blisters.
back:
* **AM:** Contain plasma exudate rich in **albumin**; raw base is **pink**.
* **PM:** Contain little fluid; raw base is pale/white; lacks vital reaction.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Pressure steam and liquids at high temperature cause blisters having plasma exudate containing albumin. Raw Skin Surface is pink... Different forms of skin vital reactions... can easily be detected both by naked eye as well as microscopy.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: A corpse from a house fire shows sooty particles in the bronchi and 70% CO saturation. Diagnosis?
back:
* **Ante-mortem fire exposure**.
* Proof: Inhalation of smoke/CO requires active respiration during the fire.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach and the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood and other tissue like bone-marrow are strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
coreConcept: Aging of Burn via Repair Signs
front: Q: Based on repair processes, what is the estimated age of a burn showing pus and granulation tissue?
back:
* **Several days** old.
* Initial leucocyte infiltration occurs within few hours; infection/repair follow over subsequent days.
citation: Page 62 (Book Page): [After few hours, there will be leucocytes infiltration and area may readily get infected followed by. appearance of pus and granulation tissue.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
coreConcept: Rule of Nines in Forensic Assessment
front: Q: What tool is utilized during forensic certification to calculate the extent of body surface area burnt?
back:
* The **Rule of Nine**.
* Used to estimate percentage area for prognosis and legal grading.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [During forensic certification, Medical Examiner takes advantage of the rule of nine to calculate the extent and percentage area involved bearing bums of the body surface.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Why is 'Pugilistic Attitude' considered a non-specific finding for ante-mortem nature?
back:
* It is a physical effect of **heat coagulation** on muscle proteins.
* It occurs in both AM and PM states as the body is exposed to intense heat.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Dead body acquires a specific boxer attitude called pugilistic attitude due to heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscle proteins. Finding has no significance, as even a dead body will attain it.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: How is an extra-dural heat hematoma differentiated from a traumatic extra-dural hematoma?
back:
* **Heat Hematoma:** Light in color, **honeycomb appearance**.
* Found directly under the site of an external head burn.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [extra-dural heat hematoma, in the immediate vicinity of external burn of head; hematoma is light in color and has a honeycomb appearance.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Describe the chronologic order of complications and death following a severe thermal burn.
back:
* 1. **Immediate:** Primary shock (pain).
* 2. **Early (24-36h):** Secondary shock (fluid loss) or toxemia.
* 3. **Delayed:** Infection and septicemia.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Immediate primary shock due to pain; Secondary shock... Death occurs: either within 24-36 hours due to toxemia... or after many days, due to infection and septicemia.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Describe the typical naked-eye appearance of a vital line of reddening in ante-mortem flame burns.
back:
* A **well-marked reddening**.
* Approximately **1/4 inch in width**, bordering the burn lesion.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Naked eye: Heated objects and flame produce well marked reddening, 1/4 inch in width, bordering the lesion.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What are the progressive physical stages of a thermal skin lesion related to time?
back:
* Immediate: Erythema/Redness.
* Delayed (hours): Blistering/Vesicles.
* Few hours: Leucocyte infiltration.
* Days: Infection, pus, and granulation tissue.
citation: Page 62 (Book Page): [Progressive stages of thermal lesion are redness, which appears at once, followed by blistering of skin, which takes some time to appear... After few hours, there will be leucocytes infiltration and area may readily get infected followed by appearance of pus and granulation tissue.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of enzyme histochemistry in distinguishing ante-mortem from post-mortem burns.
back:
* Peripheral increase in enzymes indicates vital reaction.
* Occurs earlier than histological changes.
* Remains stable despite post-mortem delay.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Increase in enzyme reaction at the periphery of the burn, which can be detected much earlier than histological changes. ... reactions are stable to withstand period of delay betweenn death and postmortem examination.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Contrast the contents and base appearance of ante-mortem versus post-mortem blisters.
back:
* Ante-mortem: Contains plasma/albumin, pink raw base.
* Post-mortem: Contains air/gas, dull white or dry base, lacks vital reaction.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Table 6.6: Pressure steam and liquids at high temperature cause blisters having plasma exudate containing albumin. Raw Skin Surface is pink.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Which specific findings in the respiratory tract prove a burn catastrophe was ante-mortem?
back:
* Presence of black sooty particles in the trachea/bronchi.
* Blood carbon monoxide (CO) levels exceeding 70%.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach and the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood and other tissue like bone-marrow are strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: List the four specific enzymes studied to identify a burn's vital reaction.
back:
1. Alkaline phosphatase
2. Acid phosphatase
3. Leucine amino-peptidase
4. Non-specific esterase
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Chosen study enzymes were alkaline phosphatase, acid phosphatase, Leucine amino-peptidase and non-specific esterase.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What defines a 'vital reaction' in skin subjected to heated objects or flame?
back:
* A well-marked zone of reddening.
* Width: Approximately 1/4 inch.
* Bordering the lesion periphery.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Table 6.6: Heated objects and flame produce well marked reddening, 1/4 inch in width, bordering the lesion.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: How is a heat-induced post-mortem 'extra-dural hematoma' differentiated from a traumatic one?
back:
* Heat-induced: Light color, honeycomb appearance.
* Site: In the vicinity of external head burns.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Postmortem artifact... extra-dural heat hematoma, in the immediate vicinity of external burn of head; hematoma is light in color and has a honeycomb appearance.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Differentiate skin splits caused by heat from ante-mortem incised wounds.
back:
* Heat splits: Caused by protein coagulation, irregular, dry base, no vital reaction.
* Incised wounds: Clean-cut, bleeding, vital reaction present.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Postmortem artifact... are flaking bone fracture & protein coagulation and bends at joints, skin splits for the same reason...]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What role does 'leucocyte infiltration' play in the histological dating of burns?
back: Indicates survival for at least a few hours post-injury; signifies a microscopic vital reaction.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Table 6.6: Burnt skin shows leucocytes infiltration, provided the lesion is not of full thickness.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Define the characteristic 'boxer attitude' seen in burnt corpses and its significance.
back:
* Name: Pugilistic attitude.
* Mechanism: Heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscle proteins.
* Significance: Post-mortem artifact; occurs in any body exposed to high heat.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Dead body acquires a specific boxer attitude called pugilistic attitude due to heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscle proteins. Finding has no significance, as even a dead body will attain it.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What is the primary naked-eye vital reaction indicating an ante-mortem burn?
back: A well-marked reddening (erythema), approximately 1/4 inch in width, bordering the burnt lesion.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Heated objects and flame produce well marked reddening, 1/4 inch in width, bordering the lesion]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: How does enzyme histochemistry distinguish ante-mortem from post-mortem burns?
back: Increased enzyme reactions (e.g., alkaline phosphatase) at the burn periphery appear much earlier than microscopic histological changes.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Increase in enzyme reaction at the periphery of the burn, which can be detected much earlier than histological changes.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Contrast the fluid content of ante-mortem versus post-mortem burn blisters.
back: Ante-mortem blisters contain plasma exudate rich in albumin; post-mortem blisters lack vital reactions and biochemical markers.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Pressure steam and liquids at high temperature cause blisters having plasma exudate containing albumin.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: In a charred body, which internal findings confirm the victim was alive during the fire?
back: Black sooty particles in the trachea/bronchi and >70% carbon monoxide saturation in blood or bone marrow.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach and the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood and other tissue like bone-marrow are strong evidence of an ante- mortem catastrophe.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Which specific enzymes are used to determine the age of a burn through histochemistry?
back: Alkaline phosphatase, acid phosphatase, leucine amino-peptidase, and non-specific esterase.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Chosen study enzymes were alkaline phosphatase, acid phosphatase, Lucien amino-peptidase and non-specific esterase.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What are the two mandatory parameters for forensic certification of burn severity?
back:
1. Extent of body surface involved (Rule of Nine).
2. Depth of the burn (superficial vs. full thickness).
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Medico-legal certification important criteria of thermal burn are extent of body surface involved and depth of the burn.]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: How long can a dead body produce a 'vital reaction' simulation if exposed to heat?
back: Up to ten to twelve hours after death, as skin cells remain viable for a variable period.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [In the case of skin, the period is about ten to twelve hours. Wright (1850) pointed out that as long as the dead body is still warm, the fire flame effect of skin is similar to that of observed during life]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: Differentiate post-mortem 'heat ruptures' from ante-mortem lacerations in burn victims.
back: Heat ruptures show no vital reaction, lack marginal bruising, and are caused by post-mortem protein coagulation.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Postmortem artifact which are produced during fire needs recognition and they are flaking bone fracture & protein coagulation... skin splits for the same reason]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What microscopic feature determines a burn is at least several hours old?
back: The presence of leucocyte infiltration into the tissue, provided the burn is not full-thickness.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Burnt skin shows leucocytes infiltration, provided the lesion is not of full thickness]

category: Determine age of burn and ante-mortem/post mortem nature of burn
front: Q: What is the defining characteristic of a burn caused by pressure steam or scalds?
back: Extensive vesication (blistering) containing albuminous fluid, usually without singeing of hair or carbon deposits.
citation: Page 62 (Book Page): [Liquid at high temperature and pressure burns lesion, on the other hand, show extensive size vesications. Both clothes and hair do not show burning or singeing.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: List the three progressive morphological stages of a thermal burn lesion.
back:
* Redness: Appears immediately.
* Blistering (Vesication): Takes some time to appear.
* Roasted patches or carbonization: Follows severe exposure.
citation: Page 62 (Book Page): [Progressive stages of thermal lesion are redness, which appears at once, followed by blistering of skin, which takes some time to appear... roasted patches at leg, groin, abdomen and vital demarcating line.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Describe the physiological mechanism behind the 'pugilistic attitude' observed in burnt corpses.
back:
* Caused by heat-induced coagulation of flexor muscle proteins.
* Proteins shorten, forcing limbs into a 'boxer-like' flexed posture.
* It occurs regardless of whether the body was alive or dead.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Dead body acquires a specific boxer attitude called pugilistic attitude due to heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscle proteins. Finding has no significance, as even a dead body will attain it.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Contrast a heat-induced postmortem extradural hematoma with a traumatic antemortem hematoma.
back:
* Heat hematoma: Light color, 'honeycomb' appearance, located near external head burns.
* Traumatic hematoma: Dark red, solid, and typically associated with skull fractures.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [extra-dural hematoma, in the immediate vicinity of external burn of head; hematoma is light in color and has a honeycomb appearance.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: A corpse from a fire shows black sooty particles in the trachea. Interpret this finding.
back:
* Definite sign of antemortem status.
* Indicates the victim was breathing during the fire.
* Usually accompanied by CO levels >70% in blood or bone marrow.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach and the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood and other tissue like bone-marrow are strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Which specific enzyme increases at the burn periphery aid in medicolegal distinction of antemortem burns?
back:
* Alkaline phosphatase.
* Acid phosphatase.
* Leucine amino-peptidase.
* Non-specific esterase.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Chosen study enzymes were alkaline phosphatase, acid phosphatase, Lucien amino-peptidase and non-specific esterase... Increase in enzyme reaction at the periphery of the burn... can be detected much earlier than histological changes.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: List the essential internal autopsy findings of the gastrointestinal system in fatal burn cases.
back:
* Curling’s ulcers: Develop in the gastric and duodenal mucosa.
* Caused by acute systemic stress and pain.
* Marked pallor of the liver and kidneys.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Internally findings are marked pallor of liver and kidneys. Curling ulcers develop in gastric and duodenal Mucosa, which occur due to pain and stress of the burns.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Using the 'Rule of Nine', calculate the surface area for the trunk and perineum.
back:
* Front of trunk (Chest + Abdomen): 18%.
* Back of trunk (Chest + Abdomen/Buttocks): 18%.
* Perineum: 1%.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Front of chest 9%, Front of abdomen 9%, Back of chest 9%, Back of abdomen and buttocks 9%, Perineum 1%.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Differentiate between antemortem and postmortem burn blisters based on fluid content.
back:
* Antemortem: Contain plasma exudate rich in albumin.
* Postmortem: Contain only air or steam.
* Antemortem bases are pink/red; postmortem bases are hard and dry.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Pressure steam and liquids at high temperature cause blisters having plasma exudate containing albumin. Raw Skin Surface is pink... Post-mortem blisters contain air.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Explain the 'secondary shock' phase in the physiological loop of fatal burns.
back:
* Involves circulatory collapse.
* Driven by massive loss of fluids from the burnt surface.
* Leads to hemoconcentration and multi-organ failure.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Secondary shock with circulatory collapse due to loss of fluid and hemo-concentration.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: What is the primary medicolegal importance of identifying postmortem burns on a body?
back:
* Often indicates an attempt to conceal homicide.
* Used to destroy evidence of physical assault or identify.
* Requires scrutiny for absence of vital reactions.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Destruction of the murder victims body to conceal crime and climate the evidence is the oldest method. Therefore burnt corpses need careful scrutiny... from a medicolegal point of view.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: What is the mechanism behind the 'Pugilistic Attitude' found in burn autopsies?
back: * Caused by heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscle proteins. * Results in a boxer-like stance. * Occurs regardless of whether the body was dead or alive during the fire.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Dead body acquires a specific boxer attitude called pugilistic attitude due to heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscle proteins. Finding has no significance, as even a dead body will attain it.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Differentiate heat-induced 'skin splits' from ante-mortem lacerations.
back: * Heat splits: Caused by skin drying/shrinking; smooth margins; no tissue bridging. * Lacerations: Irregular margins; tissue bridging; vital reaction (bruising/bleeding) present.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Postmortem artifact which are produced by fire... skin splits... differentiated during autopsy from severe hyperemia... which occur during agonal period within minutes.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: How is a heat-induced extradural hematoma identified during autopsy?
back: * Location: Directly under external burn site of head. * Appearance: Light color (brick red). * Texture: Characteristic honeycomb or friable appearance.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [extra-dural hematoma inside the skull... in the immediate vicinity of external burn of head. Such hematoma is light in color and has a honeycomb appearance.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: A charred body is found with a fractured hyoid bone but no soot in the trachea. What is the medicolegal inference?
back: * Suggests post-mortem burning to conceal a crime. * Death was likely due to strangulation (indicated by hyoid fracture) before the fire was started.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Destruction of the murder victims body to conceal crime... therefore burnt corpse needs careful scrutiny... Photo 6.23: Another similar corpse without vital reaction, cause of death strangulation.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: What internal organ changes are typical in a burn autopsy?
back: * Liver/Kidneys: Marked pallor. * Brain: Congestion and edema. * GI Tract: Presence of Curling’s ulcers in gastroduodenal mucosa.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Internally findings are marked pallor of liver and kidneys... Curling ulcers develop in gastric and duodenal Mucosa.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: What is the primary medicolegal objective when examining a charred body?
back: * 1. Identification of the deceased. * 2. Determination of cause of death (Ante-mortem vs Post-mortem). * 3. Detecting signs of crime/poisoning hidden by burns.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [burnt corpse needs careful scrutiny... from medicolegal point of view... Destruction of the murder victims body to conceal crime.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Describe the characteristic appearance of heat-induced bone fractures.
back: * Also called 'Flaking' fractures. * Characterized by irregular scaling or peeling of the outer table of the skull or long bones.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Postmortem artifact which are produced by fire... are flaking bone fracture.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Contrast the medicolegal significance of 'Soot in Trachea' vs. 'CO in Blood'.
back: * Soot in Trachea: Proves smoke inhalation (victim was breathing). * CO in Blood (>70%): Definitive chemical proof victim was alive in the fire environment.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea... and the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood... are strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: What is the medicolegal significance of 'Cigarette Burns' found during autopsy?
back: * Indicates intentional physical torture. * Often associated with custodial violence or police interrogation.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Criminal infliction of thermal burn with lit cigarette... occurs during torture by police.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: At what depth are burns classified for medicolegal certification?
back: * 1. Superficial: Not involving full skin thickness. * 2. Deep: Involving full thickness of skin and underlying tissues.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Generally two depths are referred to in the medical certificate; superficial, which does not involve full thickness of skin and others, which involve full thickness of skin and deeper tissues.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: What is the specific measurement and appearance of the external vital reaction bordering a flame burn?
back:
- Well-marked reddening.
- 1/4 inch in width.
- It borders the lesion and indicates an ante-mortem injury.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Heated objects and flame produce well marked reddening, 1/4 inch in width, bordering the lesion]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Describe the specific appearance and location of a post-mortem 'heat hematoma' during autopsy.
back:
- Light in color.
- Honeycomb appearance.
- Located extra-durally in the immediate vicinity of an external head burn.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [extra-dural heat hematoma... light in color and has a honeycomb appearance.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Why is the 'pugilistic attitude' considered a non-specific finding during a burn autopsy?
back:
- It is caused by heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscles.
- It has no medico-legal significance as it develops in both living and dead bodies.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Dead body acquires a specific boxer attitude called pugilistic attitude due to heat coagulation... Finding has no significance, as even a dead body will attain it.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Diagnosis: An autopsy reveals black soot in the stomach and 75% CO in the blood. Provide the forensic inference.
back:
- Confirms an ante-mortem catastrophe.
- Proves the victim was alive and breathing/swallowing during the fire.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach and the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood... are strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: According to the timeline of burn mortality, what usually causes death 24-36 hours post-injury?
back:
- Toxemia.
- Caused by the production of toxins by the burnt tissue.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Death occurs either within 24-36 hours due to toxemia (production of toxins by burnt tissue)]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: List the four enzymes used in histochemistry to detect ante-mortem burns before histological changes appear.
back:
- Alkaline phosphatase.
- Acid phosphatase.
- Leucine amino-peptidase.
- Non-specific esterase.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Chosen study enzymes were alkaline phosphatase, acid phosphatase, Lucien amino-peptidase and non-specific esterase.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Identify the characteristic "boxer-like" posture found in charred bodies during forensic autopsy.
back: Pugilistic Attitude. It is caused by heat-induced coagulation and shortening of the flexor muscle proteins.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Dead body acquires a specific boxer attitude called pugilistic attitude due to heat coagulation and shortening of flexor muscle proteins.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Describe the physiological mechanism behind the development of "Curling's ulcers" in burn victims.
back: They develop in the gastric and duodenal mucosa as a result of acute physiological stress and intense pain from thermal injury.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Curling ulcers develop in gastric and duodenal Mucosa, which occur due to pain and stress of the bum.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Contrast the blister contents of ante-mortem burns versus post-mortem heat effects.
back: Ante-mortem: Contains plasma exudate rich in albumin with a raw pink underlying surface. Post-mortem: Lacks albuminous fluid and vital inflammatory response.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Pressure steam and liquids at high temperature cause blisters having plasma exudate containing albumin. Raw Skin Surface is pink.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: A body is recovered from a fire with soot in the bronchi. Interpret this finding.
back: It is strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe. It proves the victim was alive and breathing during the fire, inhaling carbonaceous material.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach... are strong evidence of an ante-mortem catastrophe.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Which specific enzyme markers are utilized in histochemistry to identify ante-mortem burns?
back:
Increased reaction at the burn periphery of:
* Alkaline/Acid phosphatase
* Leucine amino-peptidase
* Non-specific esterase.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Chosen study enzymes were alkaline phosphatase, acid phosphatase, Lucien amino-peptidase and non-specific esterase... can be detected much earlier than histological changes.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Define the forensic classification of burn depth for medical certification.
back:
* Superficial: Does not involve full skin thickness.
* Full-thickness: Involves full skin thickness and deeper tissues.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [superficial, which does not involve full thickness of skin and others, which involve full thickness of skin and deeper tissues.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: What defines the naked-eye "Vital Line" of reddening in ante-mortem burns?
back: A well-marked area of reddening approximately 1/4 inch in width bordering the thermal lesion.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Heated objects and flame produce well marked reddening, 1/4 inch in width, bordering the lesion.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Differentiate a post-mortem heat hematoma from an ante-mortem extra-dural hematoma.
back: Post-mortem heat hematomas are light in color and display a characteristic "honeycomb" appearance, unlike solid ante-mortem clots.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [extra-dural hematoma, in the immediate vicinity of external burn of head; hematoma is light in color and has a honeycomb appearance.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Describe the metabolic/physiological loop of "Secondary Shock" in thermal injuries.
back: It involves circulatory collapse precipitated by massive loss of fluid and subsequent hemoconcentration.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Secondary shock with circulatory collapse due to loss of fluid and hemo-concentalion]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: What carboxy-hemoglobin level in the blood is diagnostic of an ante-mortem fire death?
back: A concentration of more than 70% carbon monoxide in the blood and tissues like bone-marrow.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood and other tissue like bone-marrow are strong evidence of an ante- mortem catastrophe.]

category: Classify electrical injuries injuries-low voltage and high voltage
front: Q: Classify the common voltage ranges for domestic and industrial electrical accidents.
back:
- Domestic: 220–240V.
- Industrial (including railways): 600V–1200V.
- Transmission lines: 11KV.
citation: Page 65 (Book Page): [Different electricity voltages are used in Pakistan; domestic from 220-240V, industry including railways 600V-1200V and transmission lines 11KV.]

category: Classify electrical injuries injuries-low voltage and high voltage
front: Q: Contrast the physiological muscle response between domestic and industrial voltage contact.
back:
- Domestic (220-240V): 'Hold-on effect' due to continuous muscle spasm.
- Industrial (600V-1200V): 'Throw-off effect' characterized by violent repulsion.
citation: Page 65 (Book Page): ['Hold-on effect' at 220-240V (domestic) causes muscle spasm... 'Throw-off effect' at 600V-1200V (industrial) short period of contact.]

category: Classify electrical injuries injuries-low voltage and high voltage
front: Q: Differentiate the cardiac outcomes of low voltage versus high voltage electrical injuries.
back:
- Low Voltage: Myocardial fibrillation (direct action on pacemaker/conducting system).
- High Voltage: Asystole or spasmodic contraction.
citation: Page 65 (Book Page): [i) Low voltage produces myocardial fibrillation... ii) High voltage either causes heart muscle to fibrillate or then becomes nonfunctional or produces spasmodic contraction and asystole.]

category: Classify electrical injuries injuries-low voltage and high voltage
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of a 'hold-on effect' in a domestic electrical accident.
back:
- Occurs at 220-240V.
- Current causes tetanic muscle spasm.
- Victim is unable to release the live conductor.
citation: Page 65 (Book Page): ['Hold-on effect' at 220-240V (domestic) causes muscle spasm, responsible for non-release of live wire.]

category: Classify electrical injuries injuries-low voltage and high voltage
front: Q: Why do electrical thermal lesions typically occur at the palms and soles?
back:
- These areas offer higher electrical resistance.
- High resistance converts electrical energy into heat.
- Results in localized thermal burns at contact points.
citation: Page 65 (Book Page): [palm and sole... offer relatively more resistance and generates heat causing thermal lesion at point of contact.]

category: Classify electrical injuries injuries-low voltage and high voltage
front: Q: List the diagnostic features of a 'loose contact' (spark) electrical lesion.
back:
- Central parchment area.
- Surrounding hyperemia.
- Pitted metallization (metallic particles embedded in tissue).
citation: Page 66 (Book Page): [Loose contact lesion... area of dry burn... central parchment surrounded by hyperemia. Microscopically... showing multiple pricked or pitted metallization.]

category: Classify electrical injuries injuries-low voltage and high voltage
front: Q: Identify the most dangerous electrical pathway through the human body and its mechanism.
back:
- Pathway: Head to either foot (e.g., lightning).
- Mechanism: Direct involvement of the brain stem.
- Effect: Fatal injury to vital cardiac and respiratory centers.
citation: Page 65 (Book Page): [iv) From head to either foot as normally happens in lightening involves brain stem having vital cardiac and respiratory centers is the most dangerous.]

category: Classify electrical injuries injuries-low voltage and high voltage
front: Q: Distinguish 'firm contact' lesions from 'industrial high voltage' lesions by appearance.
back:
- Firm Contact: Raised blisters containing gas/fluid; white slough with red rim.
- Industrial: Arcing flash burns; 'crocodile skin' appearance; massive carbonization.
citation: Page 66 (Book Page): [Firm contact lesion... raised blister... white slough surrounded by a rim of bright red... Industrial lesion... Arcing... flash burns... crocodile skin to completely carbonized tissue.]

category: Classify electrical injuries injuries-low voltage and high voltage
front: Q: Define the 'arcing effect' associated with high-tension transmission lines.
back:
- Occurs at extremely high voltage (e.g., 11KV).
- Current jumps to a person approaching the wire.
- Produces extensive flash burns without physical contact.
citation: Page 66 (Book Page): [arcing, which actually does not require contact... Arcing effect to an approaching person produces flash burns.]

category: Classify electrical injuries injuries-low voltage and high voltage
front: Q: What is 'metallization' in the context of electrical forensic examination?
back:
- Deposition of microscopic metallic particles from the conductor.
- Found embedded in the superficial cells of the epidermis.
- Characteristic of loose contact/spark lesions.
citation: Page 66 (Book Page): [metallization with metallic particles liberated from the conductor, which get embedded in the tissue.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: List two internal organ gross findings characteristic of a fatal burn autopsy.
back:
• Marked pallor of the liver.
• Marked pallor of the kidneys.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Internally findings are marked pallor of liver and kidneys.

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Describe the diagnostic significance of 'Curling Ulcers' in a burn victim's autopsy.
back:
• Found in gastric or duodenal mucosa.
• Result from physiological stress and pain.
• Indicates the burn was ante-mortem.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Curling ulcers develop in gastric and duodenal Mucosa, which occur due to pain and stress of burns.

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Distinguish an ante-mortem heat rupture from a mechanical lacerated wound during autopsy.
back:
• Heat ruptures show no vital reaction or bruising.
• Intact nerves and vessels cross the gap in heat splits.
• Lacerations show tissue bridging and bruising.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Postmortem artifact which are produced by fire... skin splits due to the same reason... differentiated during autopsy from hyperemia.

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: A charred corpse shows a honeycomb-textured, light-colored extradural hematoma. Interpret this finding.
back:
• It is a post-mortem heat artifact.
• Caused by intense heat to the skull.
• Must not be mistaken for trauma-induced hematoma.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): extra-dural hematoma in the immediate vicinity of external burn of head. This hematoma is light in color and has a honeycomb appearance.

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Identify three specific medico-legal contexts for burns mentioned in forensic practice.
back:
• Police torture (cigarette burns/elevated temperature).
• Accidental (domestic or industrial).
• Criminal destruction of a corpse to conceal evidence.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): criminal inflicting of thermal burn with lit cigarette or elevated temperature occurs during torture by police. ... Destruction of the murder victims body to conceal crime and eliminate the evidence.

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: What findings in the respiratory tract confirm a victim was alive when a fire started?
back:
• Presence of black sooty particles in the trachea and bronchi.
• Carbon monoxide levels >70% in blood or bone marrow.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach and the presence of more than 70% carbon monoxide in blood and other tissue like bone-marrow are strong evidence of an ante- mortem catastrophe.

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Apply the 'Rule of Nine' to a victim with burns covering the entire front of the trunk.
back:
• Front of Chest: 9%.
• Front of Abdomen: 9%.
• Total: 18%.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Front of chest 9%... Front of abdomen 9%.

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: A body found in a fire has a larynx Speared from burning. What does this suggest?
back:
• Suggests possible manual strangulation or suffocation prior to burning.
• The obstruction (cloth or chin overlap) protected the cavity from heat.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page)-65: cause of death suffocation by cloths stuffed in mouth, which got speared from burning being in oral cavity. ... cause of death strangulation... which got speared from burning by chin overlap.

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: What is the chronological progression of systemic complications leading to death in burn victims?
back:
• Immediate: Primary shock (pain).
• 24-36 Hours: Toxemia or secondary shock (fluid loss).
• Delayed: Infection and septicemia.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Immediate primary shock due to pain... Secondary shock with circulatory collapse... Death occurs either within 24-36 hours due to toxemia... or after many days, due to infection and septicemia.

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Describe the skeletal 'artifact' typical of post-mortem fire exposure in a forensic autopsy.
back:
• Flaking bone fractures.
• Caused by intense heat coagulation.
• Occurs without vital reaction.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): Postmortem artifact which are produced by fire... are flaking bone fracture & protein coagulation and bends at joints.

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Which specific internal organs show marked pallor during a burn victim's autopsy?
back:
- Liver
- Kidneys
- These organs typically exhibit significant pallor upon internal examination.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Internally findings are marked pallor of liver and kidneys.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Describe the morphological appearance and cause of post-mortem skin splits in fire victims.
back:
- Appearance: Resemble incised wounds/lacerations.
- Mechanism: Caused by heat-induced protein coagulation and tissue contraction.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Postmortem artifact... skin splits for the same reason (protein coagulation) and extra-dural hematoma...]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Contrast the medicolegal significance of finding soot in the trachea versus the stomach.
back:
- Trachea: Confirms ante-mortem inhalation of smoke.
- Stomach: Confirms the victim swallowed debris during the fire, also indicating ante-mortem status.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): [Presence of black sooty particles in trachea, bronchi and stomach... are strong evidence of an ante- mortem catastrophe.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: A charred body shows no soot in the airways but has a distinct ligature mark. Inference?
back:
- Probable homicidal strangulation followed by post-mortem burning to conceal the crime.
- Lack of vital soot confirms death occurred before the fire.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Destruction of the murder victims body to conceal crime and eliminate the evidence is an oldest method. Therefore burnt corpses need careful scrutiny...]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: What metabolic/pathological process causes death in burn victims between 24–36 hours post-injury?
back:
- Toxemia.
- Resulting from the production and systemic release of toxins by the burnt tissues.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Death occurs: either within 24-36 hours due to toxemia (production of toxins by burnt tissue)]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Define 'Deep Burns' according to medicolegal certification criteria.
back:
- Burns involving the full thickness of the skin.
- These extend into and damage deeper underlying tissues.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Generally two depths are referred to in the medical certificate... others, which involve full thickness of skin and deeper tissues.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Why is the 'pugilistic attitude' considered a non-specific finding in fire deaths?
back:
- It is a post-mortem artifact.
- It results solely from heat coagulation of muscle proteins and occurs even if a dead body is placed in fire.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Dead body acquires a specific boxer attitude called pugilistic attitude... Finding has no significance, as even a dead body will attain it.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Differentiate agonal mucosal changes from true ante-mortem inflammatory reactions in burns.
back:
- Ante-mortem: Marked hyperemia and leukocyte infiltration.
- Agonal artifact: Superficial mucosal erosions occurring within minutes of death without inflammatory cell infiltration.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [They are brown, irregular and superficial and should be differentiated during autopsy from hyperemia, even superficial erosion, which develop during agonal period within minutes.]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: Describe the specific appearance of heat-induced bone fractures at autopsy.
back:
- Known as 'flaking bone fractures'.
- Caused by the direct drying and brittle nature of bones exposed to extreme heat.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Postmortem artifact... are flaking bone fracture & protein coagulation and bends at joints]

category: Describe autopsy findings and medico legal importance of burns
front: Q: List the two essential criteria for forensic certification of thermal burns.
back:
1. Extent of body surface area involved (using Rule of Nines).
2. Depth of the burn (Superficial vs. Full thickness).
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Medico-legal certification important criteria of thermal burn are extent of body surface involved and depth of the burn.]

category: Classify electrical injuries injuries-low voltage and high voltage
